bull.t: Double-Digit Revenue Growth and Expanding CGM Access
bull.b: Double-digit quarterly growth, higher full-year guidance and broader reimbursement support indicate durable expansion in the addressable CGM market. Wider payer coverage can improve access for type 2 patients and support recurring sensor demand over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Strong Margin Expansion and Operating Leverage
bull.b: The 400-basis-point gross-margin improvement and higher operating margin show meaningful scale benefits as Dexcom grows. Management’s raised margin targets suggest profitability gains may persist, provided product launches and manufacturing investments remain well controlled.

bull.t: Robust Cash Generation and Lower Leverage
bull.b: Strong cash conversion gives Dexcom resources to fund manufacturing capacity, product development and strategic initiatives without relying heavily on debt. Lower leverage further improves financial flexibility, although free-cash-flow growth has recently moderated.

bear.b: A sustained slowdown would make future growth more dependent on new indications, reimbursement wins and product adoption. It could also limit additional operating leverage and reduce confidence that recent margin expansion will continue at the same pace.

Medicare access could materially expand the eligible CGM population, but delayed timing or restrictive conditions would defer that opportunity. Uncertainty also complicates patient acquisition planning and leaves an important medium-term growth catalyst outside Dexcom’s control.

bear.t: Manufacturing Ramp and Product Execution Risk
bear.b: New Irish capacity should support long-term supply, but ramp costs can pressure margins before utilization improves. Any recurrence of quality or out-of-box failures could also increase warranty expense, disrupt customer experience and slow adoption.
